transaction_protocol.attempt_directory: <output_stem>.c42_txn/attempt_<three_digit_attempt>/, where output_stem is the registered path before the .pt/.json/.commit.json suffixes
transaction_protocol.exclusive_parent_lock: The exact lock path is <output_stem>.c42_txn/namespace.lock, outside every attempt directory but inside the registered output namespace. Before inspecting or creating an attempt, the parent opens this registered regular non-symlink lock and holds an exclusive flock through child wait, validation and commit. It passes a duplicate of the same locked file descriptor to the child with pass_fds, and the child retains it until process exit. If the parent dies while the child runs, the child therefore preserves liveness exclusion; a recovery parent may classify or recover the attempt only after acquiring the lock. A second parent may wait or inspect after lock acquisition but may never allocate another attempt while the prior attempt is live or unclassified.
transaction_protocol.deterministic_run_id: SHA256 of strict canonical JSON containing collection commit, the user-visible parent argv receipt, assignment hash, checkpoint/source/runtime-asset manifests, canonical paths, seed, replicate and run_num_envs. It excludes all derived child argv, attempt directories and attempt ids, remains identical across an allowed pre-boundary retry, and prevents self-reference.
transaction_protocol.deterministic_attempt_id: SHA256 of strict canonical JSON plus a trailing newline for {attempt_number:<monotonically increasing integer>,run_id:<deterministic run id>}; it is unique for each permanent attempt directory and has no ambiguous string concatenation.
transaction_protocol.parent_import_rule: The parent may import stdlib, torch and CPU artifact validators but must never import isaacsim, omni, pxr, isaaclab.app, AppLauncher, or the child module.
transaction_protocol.child_rule: The child is the only AppLauncher owner, must validate the sealed parent intent, run id, attempt id and inherited lock capability. Immediately after validating the inherited locked descriptor it sets FD_CLOEXEC while retaining the descriptor itself until child exit, preventing Kit or other exec descendants from leaking the namespace lock. It must not import the parent canonical publisher or contain canonical path constants. Every child write API receives a stage-only capability whose resolved targets must remain below the sealed attempt directory and reject symlinks, traversal and injected canonical paths.
transaction_protocol.durable_write_primitive: Write a same-directory temporary regular file with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, flush and fsync it, hard-link it no-clobber to the registered final marker name, fsync the directory, and retain both evidence and hashes; reject symlinks and non-regular files.

transaction_protocol.boundary_semantics: authoritative_env_step creates and fully fsyncs 20_first_step_armed.json only when progress.first_env_step_invoked is false, then sets that flag true and enters the first env.step; later steps do not write the marker again. Marker existence or corruption is conservatively post-boundary and never retryable. A caught 05 or 18 failure, or an abrupt pre-boundary child/parent death before either receipt, may permit retry only when 20 and every later child/staged/canonical-success object (30, 31, 32, 40, 45, 46, 55, 56, 60 and the canonical artifact pair/commit) are absolutely absent. For 05, Popen must never have succeeded and no child PID or inherited lock holder may exist. For a spawn-successful abrupt failure, the original parent must have waited for child exit, or a recovery parent must have acquired namespace.lock after the child-held duplicate was released; 50 then records the available raw wait status or null recovery status, logs and observed 10/15 markers, and 70 records boundary_armed=false and retry_permitted=true. Caught 18 may additionally have 19; all retryable branches may have parent-written 50/70. Any other child/staged evidence is non-retryable.
transaction_protocol.attempt_sequence_validation: Attempt directories are a gap-free sequence starting at 001. Before allocating or accepting attempt N, the lock-holding parent and analyzer validate every lower attempt: its attempt-local 70 and canonical failure receipt are samefile/hash-identical, boundary_armed is false, retry_permitted is true, and no staged or canonical-success evidence belonging to or cryptographically bound to that lower attempt exists. Namespace-global canonical artifacts belonging to the final higher attempt are not attributed to a lower attempt. A lower non-retryable or conflicting attempt rejects the candidate. A successful or publication-recovery attempt must be the highest and final attempt; any higher-numbered attempt, gap or unclassified prior attempt rejects.
child_failure_order: before boundary: capture Python error, write 18_child_preboundary_failed.json, optionally write 19_close_requested_preboundary.json, then close
after boundary and before prepared: capture Python error, write 45_child_failed.json, write 46_close_requested_failure.json, then close
after prepared: write 46_close_requested_failure.json without 45, producing an explicit conflict with 32 that parent rejects, then close
parent_success_requirements: waitpid reports WIFEXITED and exact exit code zero with no signal
started, app-started, first-step, prepared and success close-requested markers form one valid hash chain and every failure marker is absent
staged hashes, sizes, schemas, assignment, trace, action algebra, plan, checkpoints, sources and runtime assets validate independently after child exit

transaction_protocol.hash_chain: Every arrow A <- B means the later receipt B contains the SHA-256 of predecessor A; an earlier object never predicts or binds a future receipt. transaction_protocol.failure_classification: Any marker conflict, missing post-boundary evidence, staged corruption, nonzero or signaled exit, post-exit authority drift, validator failure, or canonical collision produces attempt-local 70_parent_failed.json and its canonical failure-receipt hardlink.
